decisions.reason: Fair. A schema revision had no approval path. The spec now says a revision is made as a change to the tracked file through the plan and decision process, and the library takes it into use with a new governed action, schema-adopt, with a preview digest, the reshelving list, all four levels, default block, and an acceptance criterion. The library table has the new row.

Fair. Placement names a home shelf for counting and now files nothing by itself. The rules of the shelf whose crawl found the candidate decide whether it is filed, a book whose home shelf has no rules counts there without activating it, and a candidate those rules refuse is not filed whatever its primary topic. Added to the placement section and the criteria.

Not part of this change. The demand-derived external queries, the owner not reviewing wanted-topic text, the admitted limit of the filter, the logged and dismissible queries and the off switch are earlier statements the owner agreed. I did not touch them. I will tell the owner that it is an accepted risk they may want to revisit.

Right that the destination rule was thin, though it predates this change. The spec now allows only http and https, resolves every hop including redirects, refuses private, loopback, link-local, unspecified, multicast and reserved addresses in any encoding, and checks the resolved address again at connection time. The criterion was updated to match.

Real gap in my text. A shelf now has two scopes that need not match: the schema sentence for placement and a fetch scope in the rules for the crawler and relevance, starting from the schema sentence, with the library report showing where they differ. The limits list and the scope-change statement use the fetch scope.

The gap predates this change, but the claim should be enforceable. Added a proposed statement that a visibility change takes effect at once, because every query uses the visible subset as it is at that moment and nothing is kept per token beyond the request, plus a criterion. Whether any cache exists is a later design matter for the owner.

The agreed statement said an edit takes effect only after reapproval but not what runs meanwhile. Added that the host keeps each approved version as a snapshot bound to its digest, the crawler reads the snapshot and never the edited file, and the shelf pauses if the snapshot is missing. A criterion covers it.

My contradiction. Dormant now means no operational rules file and no state, and the archived record of a retired shelf rules is explicitly not operational and does not count, so retiring a shelf returns it to dormant consistently.
